RedHeron is the user name for Ray Jenson. Mr. Jenson is a writer who has been a fan of Robert Jordan's works since the Conan days.

Born in Utah, Ray moved around a lot as a child, gaining a breadth of knowledge that could only be useful to a spermatophile or a writer. Being that spermatophiles don't tend to make a living simply knowing lots of inane things, Ray began writing. He completed his first story at the age of five.

At the age of nine years old, Ray entered his first writing contest, one which was intended as a competition between adults. Though he initially won fourth place in the city-wide contest, this award was later reduced to Honorable Mention when his age was discovered. He didn't make a fuss about it, because they didn't take away the prize money of fifty dollars.

At the age of twelve, Ray wrote his first novel. However, it was simply not publishable at the time (and still isn't, because it's really crap). His grandmother bought him an electric typewriter, which he thought was really cool, but which seemed to run out of correction tape about every other day. Ray soon learned the art of not being a perfectionist.

At the age of thirteen, Ray entered a poetry contest at his school, but his poem was disqualified because it was four lines too long. However, even though disqualified, it was published in the yearbook. Ray was kinda stoked about that.

Ray's first actual professional writing was at the age of sixteen, when he sold his writing skills to classmates in an entrepreneurial class (on the advice of the teacher) so that the business plan would sound more professional. This, however, was short-lived, as only one member of the class actually ever got a business running, using a business plan that Ray didn't have a thing to do with.

At age eighteen, Ray took a couple of odd jobs writing freelance for a literary magazine. By age twenty, Ray had become a staff writer at another. By age twenty-two, Ray found himself at the helm, as an assistant editor-in-chief. Spending all of his time managing the other writers and operating the magazine took its toll, and Ray ended his association with the magazine at the age of twenty-five (the magazine closed its doors only a year later).

Ray next took a low-level job flowing in the text in textbooks. Though he loved the job, he discovered that he was actually allergic to the paper dust (as opposed to the magazine, where almost everything was electronically done or done by someone else). A year later, Ray was forced to quit. However, Ray loved writing, and so picked that up again. However, he got a bad agent whose only skill appeared (to Ray, at least) to be throwing the five-year contract in Ray's face whenever Ray tried to place pressure on her. So, for five years, Ray's work never got past the agent into the outside world.

At the age of twenty-seven, Ray married, only to end the marriage eighteen months later as it turned out to be a bad idea to marry someone who is mentally ill and unable to cope with the mental illness of a spouse (well... this describes Ray, too, so let's be fair: it was all her fault). Ray still blames 9/11 for a lot of his problems, including his inability to get work outside of writing. Of course, this is simply an excuse to buy time with the landlord. Ray's son still doesn't forgive him for leaving. And yes, it's sad, but it was for the best. Having a child to take care of when you can't even care for yourself is no way to be a parent.

Now in his thirties, Mr. Jenson is now working on several writing projects, including two that are related to the Wheel of Time series, and four which have nothing whatsoever to do with the Wheel of Time (well, except for the whole 'fiction' genre being applicable... but you get the drift). He is also the proud father to a daughter, the mother of whom is the love of his life. With Ray's belief that the whole marriage thing in general is a bad idea, he's still considering making the mistake again, though with a little more care this time.

But keep your hands off his computer.
